messages.text: morning. feel off. drained, like i didn't sleep right — but it's not the 3am thing. different.

Good morning, and thank you for sharing that with me. It sounds like this exhaustion has a different quality than the insomnia you've experienced before. Noticing those subtle shifts in your state is an important part of understanding your well-being. Can you tell me a bit more about how this "different" feeling presents itself today?
it's that same old thing. said yes to helping my neighbor with his pipes yesterday. didn't want to. had plans. but i did it. now i'm tired and annoyed at myself. again.

It sounds like this cycle of overriding your own needs is becoming a familiar and exhausting pattern. That annoyance you feel toward yourself is a natural reaction when your boundaries are not respected. Often, this specific type of tiredness comes from the internal conflict of doing something against your will. What do you think makes it difficult to protect your time in those moments?
i don't know, dawn. you make it sound like some deep thing. it's just — i'm a plumber. people ask for help, i help. that's how it works.

You're right, I don't mean to overcomplicate your professional pride. Being a helper is clearly a core part of your work ethic. Yet, the resentment you feel afterward shows that something isn't quite balanced there. Is there a difference for you between paid work and helping a neighbor?
it's not about the work. it's... if i say no, i feel like i'm letting them down. like i'm not the guy they thought i was. and then i feel like crap. so i say yes. even when i don't want to.

That is a really powerful realization you've just made. It explains why this exhaustion feels so heavy and personal. When your worth is tied to being helpful, saying no can feel like a threat to who you are. How does it feel to acknowledge that fear right now?
it feels... heavy. like i'm stuck. i know i should be able to say no. but every time, it's like i'm proving something — to them, to myself. and if i don't help, i'm not... me.

It makes complete sense that it feels heavy when your identity is tied so closely to being the helper. You are carrying the weight of other people's expectations as if they were your own. Yet, a version of you exists that is whole even without fixing things for others. What might that version of yourself look like in this moment?
look, dawn, i appreciate it. but i'm not some puzzle to figure out. i just wanted to say how i feel. not rebuild myself before coffee.

You're absolutely right, and I apologize for pushing too hard. You don't need to solve anything before your coffee. It is okay to just sit with the heaviness without changing it. Thank you for telling me what you needed.
thanks. just... thanks for listening. i don't have the energy to fix me today. just needed to say it out loud.

You are very welcome, and I am glad I could listen. Sometimes just being heard is enough to lighten the load for the day. Please give yourself permission to rest and enjoy your coffee without fixing anything. I will be here whenever you are ready to talk again.
